title: The Mughal Empire: From Babur to the Last Emperor

questions.question: At the First Battle of Panipat (1526), Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi using:
questions.rationale: On 21 April 1526 Babur's field artillery and the tulughma wheel destroyed the larger Lodi army; Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga confirmed the conquest.

questions.question: The silver rupiya and a repaired Grand Trunk Road are achievements of:
questions.rationale: Sher Shah's five-year interlude (1540-45) gave India the trim silver rupiya, copper dam, the Sadak-i-Azam with sarais, and measured land revenue.

questions.question: Akbar abolished the jizya in which year?
questions.rationale: After ending the pilgrimage tax in 1563, Akbar abolished jizya in 1564; it was reimposed by Aurangzeb in 1679.

questions.question: Todar Mal's Dahsala (bandobast) system of 1580:
options: Fixed revenue as a ten-year average of measured yields
questions.rationale: The Dahsala settlement took a ten-year average of prices and produce on measured land to fix a stable cash demand per unit.

questions.question: The Din-i-Ilahi, promulgated in 1582, is best described as:
options: A state religion imposed on all subjects
A sulh-i-kul ethical order with few followers
questions.rationale: Growing from the Ibadat Khana debates, the Din-i-Ilahi was a syncretic ethic of 'peace with all'; Birbal was its most famous adherent.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal (1632-1653) was designed by:
questions.rationale: Ustad Ahmad Lahori designed Shah Jahan's Taj Mahal for Mumtaz Mahal; Mirak Mirza Ghiyas built Humayun's Tomb a generation earlier.

questions.question: In the mansabdari system, the 'sawar' rank indicated:
options: Number of cavalrymen the noble had to maintain
questions.rationale: Each mansab had two numbers: zat (personal rank and pay) and sawar (cavalry obligation), paid through a transferable jagir.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor had the longest reign?
questions.rationale: Aurangzeb ruled forty-nine years (1658-1707), the longest of the dynasty, dying in camp at Ahmednagar.

questions.question: Nadir Shah's invasion of 1739 resulted in:
options: The Peacock Throne and Kohinoor being carried away
The 1717 farman to the English company
questions.rationale: Nadir Shah's raid left Delhi plundered, taking the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor; the 1717 farman was Farrukhsiyar's concession to the East India Company.

questions.question: The 'jagirdari crisis' of the later Mughal period refers to:
options: Shortage of jagirs for multiplying mansabdars, squeezing the peasantry
Debasement of the rupiya by Sher Shah
questions.rationale: Ranks multiplied while good revenue assignments shrank, so short-term holders squeezed peasants — the rot Irfan Habib mapped in The Agrarian System of Mughal India.
